newsitem.title: USA: Nike stock slumps on fears of lower production.
newsitem.headline: Nike stock slumps on fears of lower production.

text.p: The stock of Nike Inc. fell about 7 percent Monday on fears the athletic footwear giant may be bracing for a slowdown.

Nike, based in Beaverton, Ore., said it was adjusting its production capacity lower but a spokesman for the company said the move did not mean Nike was expecting sales of its hot-selling footwear and clothing to cool off.
In fact, the company said it still expects worldwide orders for the fourth quarter ending in July to be about 34 percent above the year-ago level.

Nike stock tumbled to a low of $51.25 earlier in the day after Smith Barney analyst Faye Landes reduced her rating on Nike to neutral from outperform. The stock recovered slightly to close at $54.875, down $4.25, on the New York Stock Exchange.

In a research report, Landes said during a recent trip to Asia, she learned Nike has told its plants in China and Indonesia to cut footwear production beginning in May and through June and July. She said the cuts could reduce footwear production, which accounts for two-thirds of company revenues, by over 20 percent.
Landes said the production cuts would not be offset by increased production elsewhere.
Nike spokesman Jim Small said the company did tell its non-exclusive suppliers that it would not need as much production capacity as before, but he said such moves were not unusual.
"What she is focusing on has nothing to do with a downturn in the market," he said.

He said Nike has seen such explosive growth in recent years that if it expects growth of 25 percent, for example, it might book 50 percent excess capacity in case demand is even stronger than anticipated.

Small said Nike has made no change in its future orders forecast since late March when the company predicted orders for delivery in the three months ending in July would be about 34 percent above the year-ago period.
"Future orders are still very strong at 34 percent, which in any business is tremendous growth," Small said.
The sell-off in Nike shares Monday was not the first time Nike stock has been hit by fears of a slowdown.

Last month, Nike shares were hit by unconfirmed reports that orders from several retailers had been reduced. At the time, Woolworth Corp. denied that its Foot Locker shoe retailer had cut its order from Nike.

In her report, Landes said she suspected demand in the United States might be slowing at a quicker rate than Nike had previously forecast and that the possibility of Nike maintaining the explosive growth it has seen in recent years has been significantly reduced.
However, Small said those suspicions were unfounded.
"That just doesn't hold true, there is nothing in the numbers that is backing up what she is saying," he said.
Small said the reduction in production capacity has no affect on earnings or revenue projections.
